Rashi on Shabbat 134b:11:1.hebrew: אי אמרת בשלמא ת"ק מזלפין - ביום ראשון קאמר, ולא איירי בהרחצה כלל אלא בזילוף, היינו דאתא ר"א בן עזריה ופליג ואמר מרחיצין:
Rashi on Shabbat 134b:11:1.english: Granted, if you say [that] the first tanna [says] "one may sprinkle" - [That is, he] says [one may sprinkle] on the first day, and does not speak of washing at all, rather [only] of sprinkling — this is why Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya came and disagreed and said: "One may wash."

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:11:2.hebrew: אלא אי אמרת - תנא קמא נמי מרחיצין אמר בשני הימים, ולא פליג ר"א אלא איום שלישי דקאמר ת"ק מזלפין — אף מרחיצין ביום השלישי מיבעי ליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 134b:11:2.english: However, if you say - [that] the first tanna also stated "one may wash" regarding the two days, and Rabbi Elazar only disagrees regarding the third day — where the first tanna said "one may sprinkle" — [then] he should have [stated], "one may even wash on the third day."

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:13:1.english: They were [engaged] in it - They examined it closely.

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:14:1.hebrew: דאי ס"ד הרחצת מילה מי גרע מחמין על גבי מכה - דשרי, והכא אסרי רבנן בשלישי (לגמרי):
Rashi on Shabbat 134b:14:1.english: For if it should enter your mind [that it refers to] washing [the] circumcision, is it any worse than [placing] hot water on a wound - Which is permitted, whereas here the Rabbis forbid [it] on the third [day] (completely).

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:15:1.hebrew: ולא שני כו' - והכא גבי מילה, בהוחמו בשבת עסקינן; הלכך בשלישי דליכא סכנתא, לא:
Rashi on Shabbat 134b:15:1.english: And is there no difference, etc. - And here, regarding circumcision, we are dealing with [water] that was heated on Shabbat; therefore, on the third [day], when there is no danger, [it is] not [permitted].

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:16:1.hebrew: אמר אביי אנא בעאי דאישני ליה - אני הייתי רוצה לתרץ אתקפתא זו כדשני ליה רב יוסף, מפני שסכנה היא לו:
Rashi on Shabbat 134b:16:1.english: Abaye said: I wanted to answer him - I wanted to resolve this objection as Rav Yosef answered him: because it is a danger for him.

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:16:2.hebrew: וקדם רב יוסף ושנייא ליה - דודאי מתניתין חמין שהוחמו בשבת נמי שרי בימים הראשונים, ולר"א אף בשלישי, מפני שמניעת חמין סכנה היא לו:
Rashi on Shabbat 134b:16:2.english: And Rav Yosef answered him first - For certainly [in] our Mishnah, hot water that was heated on Shabbat is also permitted on the first days, and according to Rabbi Elazar [ben Azarya], even on the third [day], because withholding hot water is a danger for him.

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:19:1.hebrew: אין נותנין כו' - קס"ד גזרה משום שחיקת סמנין כשמואל, דטעמיה משום הכי הוא, והיינו דקאמר "אבל נותן חוץ למכה", דלא מוכחא מילתא דלרפואה:
Rashi on Shabbat 134b:19:1.english: One may not place, etc. - We initially assumed [that this is] a decree on account of grinding herbs, like Shmuel, whose reason is because of this; and that is why [the baraita] says, "but one may place [it] outside the wound," because it is not evident that [it is] for healing.

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:1:1.english: And one may sprinkle on him - the hot water.

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:1:2.hebrew: ביד - אבל לא בכלי. ובגמ' פריך: הא אמרת רישא מרחיצין, דמשמע כדרכו, והדר תני אפילו לזלף עליו בכלי אסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 134b:1:2.english: By hand - but not with a vessel. And in the Gemara it asks: You said in the first clause "one may wash," which implies in its usual manner, and then it teaches [that] even to sprinkle on him with a vessel is forbidden?

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:22:1.hebrew: מוך יבש וספוג יבש - דלאו לרפואה היא, אלא שלא ישרטו בגדיו הקשים מכתו:
Rashi on Shabbat 134b:22:1.english: A dry compress and a dry sponge - For it is not for healing, but rather so that his hard garments will not scratch his wound.

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:22:2.hebrew: אבל לא כתיתין יבישים וגמי יבש - חתיכות בגדים דקות, משום דמסו, וגזרו משום שחיקת סמנין:
Rashi on Shabbat 134b:22:2.english: But not dry rags and a dry reed - [Dry rags are] thin pieces of cloth; [they are forbidden] because they heal, and [the Sages] decreed [against using them] on account of grinding medicines.

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:22:3.hebrew: קשיא כתיתין אכתיתין - רישא שרי מוך יבש, דהיינו כתיתין, וסיפא אסר כתיתין:
Rashi on Shabbat 134b:22:3.english: [There is a] difficulty [regarding] rags [versus] rags - The first clause permits a dry compress, which is rags, and the latter clause prohibits rags.

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:22:4.hebrew: חדתי - חדשים, שלא היו על גבי מכה מעולם, מסו; עתיקי לא מסו:
Rashi on Shabbat 134b:22:4.english: New [rags] - New [ones], that have never been on a wound, heal; old [ones] do not heal.

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:22:5.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr>: שמע מינה הני כתיתין מסו:
Rashi on Shabbat 134b:22:5.english: This is the reading: "Conclude from this [that] these rags heal."

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:23:1.hebrew: ערלתו ודאי דוחה השבת - דבהאי קרא "וביום השמיני", דילפינן מיניה אפילו בשבת, כתיב בסיפיה "ערלתו", דמשמע מיעוטא — ערלתו של זה ולא אחר — ולמעוטי ספק אתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 134b:23:1.english: His certain foreskin overrides Shabbat - For in this verse, "And on the eighth day" [Leviticus 12:3], from which we derive [that circumcision is performed] even on Shabbat, it is written at its end "his foreskin," which implies an exclusion: "his foreskin" — of this [one] and not another — and it comes to exclude [a case of] uncertainty.

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:2:1.hebrew: ספק - כגון ספק בן ח' חדשים [וספק בן ט'], דהוא כאבן בעלמא, ואין מילתו דוחה שבת (וספק בן ט'):
Rashi on Shabbat 134b:2:1.english: Uncertainty - For example, an uncertain eight-month [baby] [or an uncertain nine-month baby], for he is merely like a stone, and his circumcision does not override Shabbat (or an uncertain nine-month [baby]).

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:2:2.hebrew: ר' יהודה מתיר באנדרוגינוס - דאיתרבי מקראי, כדמפרש בגמ' לקמן:
Rashi on Shabbat 134b:2:2.english: Rabbi Yehuda permits [doing so] for a hermaphrodite - For he is included from verses, as [the Gemara] explains below.

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:3:1.english: And didn’t you say [in] the first clause [that] one may wash [him] - And even in its usual manner.

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:4:1.hebrew: כיצד קתני - מרחיצין דרישא לאו כדרכו הוא, דתנא סיפא לפרושי כיצד מרחיצין, כגון לזלף ביד, ואפילו ביום ראשון:
Rashi on Shabbat 134b:4:1.english: [It] teaches "How" - "One may wash [the baby]" of the first clause is not in its usual manner, for [the Tanna] taught the latter clause to explain how one washes, such as sprinkling by hand, and even on the first day.

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:6:1.hebrew: תניא כוותיה דרבא כו' - ה"ג: ביום השלישי מזלפין עליו ביד, ולא גרסינן אבל לא בכלי:
Rashi on Shabbat 134b:6:1.english: It was taught in accordance with [the opinion of] Rava, etc. - This is the [correct] reading: "On the third day, one sprinkles [water] on him by hand," and we do not read "but not with a vessel."

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:7:1.hebrew: אתאן לת"ק - הך סיפא תנא קמא אמרה, דאילו ר"א אפילו הרחצה כדרכו שרי:
Rashi on Shabbat 134b:7:1.english: We have arrived at [the opinion of] the first tanna - This latter clause was stated by the first tanna, whereas Rabbi Elazar [ben Azarya] permits even washing in its usual manner.

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:8:1.hebrew: משום דגדול לא סליק בישרא הייא - היינו טעמא דמעשה שכם לאו ראיה גמורה היא, משום דגדול אין מכה שבבשרו מעלה ארוכה מהר, אבל קטן נתרפא מידי סכנתו מהר:
Rashi on Shabbat 134b:8:1.english: Because an adult’s flesh does not heal immediately - This is the reason that the incident of Shechem is not a complete proof: because [for] an adult, the wound in his flesh does not heal quickly, whereas a child recovers from his danger quickly.

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:9:1.english: He ruled for him in accordance with his teaching - He permitted washing for him in its usual manner on the first day [after circumcision] that fell on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:9:2.hebrew: איחלש - נעשה חולה, והיה דואג שמא על כך נענש:
Rashi on Shabbat 134b:9:2.english: He became ill - He became sick, and he was worried lest he had been punished for this.

Rashi on Shabbat 134b:9:3.hebrew: אמר בהדי תרגימנא דסבי למה לי - מה היה לי לחלוק כנגד זקנים הללו, רב יהודה ורבה בר אבוה, שפירשו שאסור להרחיץ:
Rashi on Shabbat 134b:9:3.english: He said: Why [should] I [contend] with the interpretation of the Elders - What business did I have disagreeing with these Elders, Rav Yehuda and Rabbah bar Avuh, who explained that it is forbidden to wash [the baby]?

Tosafot on Shabbat 134b:14:1.hebrew: מי גרע מחמין על גבי מכה - והיכי אסרי רבנן בשלישי? אע"ג דאיכא למימר דרב אמרה למילתיה כר"א בן עזריה, דפסקינן לעיל הלכתא כוותיה, משמע ליה דלכ"ע קאמר. ועוד, דאפילו לר"א בן עזריה פריך, דמשמע דשרי בשלישי משום סכנה מדמייתי קרא "ויהי ביום השלישי", ורב איירי במכה שאין בה סכנה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 134b:14:1.english: "Is it worse than hot water on a wound?" - [That is,] how could the Rabbis forbid [washing the circumcision] on the third [day]? Even though one could say that Rav stated his ruling in accordance with Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah, whom we ruled above the halakhah follows, it seemed to [Rabbi Yaakov] that [Rav] stated [it] according to everyone. And furthermore, even according to Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah he asks [this question], for it is implied that [Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah] permits [it] on the third [day] because of danger, since he cites the verse, "And it came to pass on the third day," whereas Rav is speaking of a wound in which there is no danger.

Tosafot on Shabbat 134b:14:2.hebrew: ואין מונעין חמין ושמן - פירש ה"ר יוסף פורת בשם רבינו שמואל, דבמעורבת יחד איירי; דאי כל חד באפי נפשיה, מאי קמ"ל? בשמן, מתני' היא בפ' שמנה שרצים (לעיל שבת דף קיא.): "אבל סך הוא את השמן", והיינו אפילו על גבי מכה, מדקתני: "בני מלכים סכין ע"ג מכותיהן שמן וורד", מכלל דבשאר שמן מותר לאחר אפילו ע"ג מכה. ושמואל נמי היכי הוה פליג:
Tosafot on Shabbat 134b:14:2.english: And one does not prevent hot water and oil - Rabbi Yosef Porat explained in the name of Rabbeinu Shmuel that [Rav] is speaking of when they are mixed together; for if each one [were applied] on its own, what is [Rav] teaching us? With regard to oil, it is an [explicit] Mishnah in the chapter [entitled] Shemonah Sheratzim (above, Shabbat 111a): "Rather, one may anoint with oil," and that is even on a wound, since it teaches: "Princes may anoint rose oil on their wounds," which implies that with other [types of] oil it is permitted for anyone else even on a wound. And furthermore, how could Shmuel have disagreed?
